# DC renderer robustness & performance hardening

## Context / Problem
The DC path shells out to pandoc per field, which introduces three production
hazards proven in the DC experiment: (1) a per-field subprocess tax — latency is a
flat ~0.3s/field spawn cost independent of body size, and a serial reconcile pass
over many fields blocked ~20 min of wall time on `fork+exec`; (2) a
pathological-input hang — one corpus body drove pandoc's jira reader to spin
13.5 min at 95.8% CPU, and pypandoc invokes pandoc with no timeout, so one field
can stall the whole reconcile indefinitely; (3) pandoc is GPL and rides in the
`pypandoc-binary` wheel, so its provenance and license must be pinned and recorded.
These must be designed against before the DC codec ships live.

## Prior art / dependency boundaries (do NOT re-decide what 271c already chose)
- **The renderer module and its pandoc delivery are owned by 271c.** Story
  `[rebar:271c-e88f-3220-4c9b]` ships the pure renderer at
  `adapters/jira_family/wiki_render.py` and delivers pandoc via the
  **`pypandoc-binary` wheel** (the pandoc binary is BUNDLED IN THE WHEEL and pinned
  in `pyproject.toml`), specifically so the DC path is self-contained in CI and
  prod with no system pandoc install. This story hardens THAT module and pins THAT
  wheel; it does **not** introduce a separate system-level pandoc or an
  `acli`-style version+sha binary pin (acli is a symlink + `acli jira auth login`
  system prerequisite, not a pinned pip binary — there is no acli pin pattern to
  mirror).
- 271c leaves `WikiTextCodec` fully identity and does NOT reference `wiki_render`
  from any codec op; wiring the renderer into `to_wire` (and therefore the live
  send) is owned by the cutover story `[rebar:3388-96e8-e14e-4221]`. This story
  touches only the pure `wiki_render.py` module functions, not the codec or the
  live send.
- **The change-gated "no-op → no pandoc spawn" property is delivered by the
  cutover/echo story `[rebar:3388-96e8-e14e-4221]`**, which introduces the
  change-gated `rich_sha` render gate; that symbol does not yet exist on
  `origin/main` and is not this story's to add. THIS story owns only the cost,
  timeout, fallback, batching, and compliance of a render that IS performed.

## Approach
- **Bound the per-render subprocess cost by batching:** when a changed body IS
  rendered, batch its structurally-safe units into as few pandoc invocations as
  correctness allows rather than one spawn per unit. (pandoc 3.9 exposes no
  `--server`/daemon, confirmed, so a persistent server is out of scope; batching is
  the available lever.)
- **Hard timeout + verbatim fallback, defined coherently WITH batching:** wrap
  every pandoc invocation with a per-call wall-clock timeout. On timeout or
  non-zero exit, degrade **every unit in that invocation's batch** to its original
  Markdown verbatim (plain Markdown is trivially echo-safe), and record a per-unit
  fallback marker. Because the fallback granularity is the batch, a batch is only
  ever grown to include units whose combined failure is acceptable to degrade
  together; a unit already flagged dangerous by 271c's classifier is rendered in
  its own single-unit invocation so its verbatim fallback cannot pull safe siblings
  down with it. This removes the batching↔fallback interaction gap: batch boundary
  == fallback boundary.
- **Compliance:** pin the `pypandoc-binary` wheel by version in `pyproject.toml`
  (271c's mechanism), record the wheel-bundled pandoc's GPL license in the project
  SBOM/notice, and verify the wheel pin in CI.

## Scope
- `adapters/jira_family/wiki_render.py` — the pure DC renderer module delivered by
  271c: add the per-invocation timeout wrapper, the batch-granular verbatim
  fallback, and unit-batching (dangerous units rendered singly). No codec op and no
  live-send site is touched here.
- `pyproject.toml` — pin the `pypandoc-binary` wheel version (extends 271c's pin;
  no separate system pandoc).
- CI workflow config — verify the `pypandoc-binary` wheel pin (NOT an acli-style
  system-binary sha check).
- SBOM/licensing notice file — record the wheel-bundled pandoc GPL entry.
- `tests/` — timeout, batch-fallback, and batching tests over the vendored DC
  corpus fixture.

## Testing
- Timeout path: a synthetic input that exceeds the configured timeout falls back to
  verbatim Markdown for every unit in its batch and the render returns; asserted by
  `test_dc_pandoc_timeout_falls_back`.
- Failure path: a non-zero pandoc exit degrades that batch to plaintext without
  raising, and the fallback is recorded per unit; `test_dc_pandoc_error_degrades`.
- Batching: a body of N safe units renders in fewer than N pandoc invocations
  (spawn-count spy), while a body containing a dangerous unit renders that unit in
  its own single-unit invocation; `test_dc_render_batches_safe_units`.
- Batch==fallback boundary: when a batched invocation times out, exactly the units
  in that batch fall back to verbatim and safe units in OTHER batches still render;
  `test_dc_batch_fallback_boundary`.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Every pandoc invocation has a wall-clock timeout and, on timeout or non-zero
  exit, degrades every unit in that invocation's batch to verbatim Markdown without
  raising; the render returns; verified by `test_dc_pandoc_timeout_falls_back` and
  `test_dc_pandoc_error_degrades`.
- [ ] A changed body of N structurally-safe units renders in fewer than N pandoc
  invocations, and a dangerous unit is rendered in its own single-unit invocation
  so its verbatim fallback cannot degrade safe siblings; verified by
  `test_dc_render_batches_safe_units` and `test_dc_batch_fallback_boundary` (batch
  boundary == fallback boundary).
- [ ] The pandoc binary is provided by the `pypandoc-binary` wheel pinned by
  version in `pyproject.toml` (271c's mechanism, not a system pandoc), the wheel
  pin is verified in CI, and the wheel-bundled pandoc GPL license is recorded in
  the SBOM/notice; verified by the CI wheel-pin check and a notice-file test.
